items.title: FPL GW9 TRANSFER TIPS! | Top Picks Tier List for Gameweek 9 - 2026/27! ⭐
items.headline: Haaland is the Gameweek 9 priority as Joao Pedro and Saka injuries reshape FPL plans
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the standout buy and captaincy option for Gameweek 9, with Manchester City’s forward described as essential despite his £15.7m price. He is captainable through Gameweeks 9-11 and offers a level of reliable output few other premium assets can match. Cole Palmer remains a hold for Chelsea’s home meeting with an out-of-form Manchester United, while Bryan Mbeumo is also worth retaining despite the difficult Chelsea and Aston Villa fixtures: he continues to get chances, plays regular minutes and could retain penalties if Bruno Fernandes remains out of United’s side.

The main injury-led decision concerns Joao Pedro. His recurring knee problem is expected to rule him out of Gameweeks 9 and 10, with Gameweek 11 a possible return target. He becomes a sell if the absence is confirmed as longer-term, particularly for managers who bought him near £7.8m-£7.9m and have little value to protect. Bukayo Saka is already ruled out for at least five weeks and is an obvious sale, while Dominik Szoboszlai, Luke Shaw and Emiliano Martinez are also likely exits because of injuries. Bruno Fernandes is only worth monitoring if Manchester United appoint a new manager and he returns to the starting XI; otherwise, he should make way, especially if he blocks a move to Haaland.

Up front, Nicolas Jackson is a strong buy at £6.7m after his recent form and with favourable enough fixtures to sustain it. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is a cheaper, dependable alternative thanks to penalties, secure minutes and acceptable fixtures. Igor Thiago and Barry are holds rather than purchases: Thiago has penalties and 90-minute security but lacks value, while Barry’s strong underlying numbers, Newcastle and Coventry fixtures, and £5.6m price justify patience despite a recent drop. Gonzalo and Wissa are sales after poor form, reduced minutes and tougher schedules, while Evanilson carries a growing rotation risk following the return of Kroupi Jr.

In midfield, Manzambi is the leading transfer target. His 3.8 shots per game despite averaging only 73 minutes, combined with Aston Villa’s strong fixture run, make him a high-upside pick. Pascal Gross remains a priority hold or buy even against Manchester City: he has penalties, secure minutes and Brighton’s attack is strong enough to trouble City. Tavernier is also a buy, though reduced set-piece involvement places him behind Manzambi and Gross. At the back, Antonio Silva is the preferred defensive signing, offering clean-sheet potential, defensive contributions, bonus points and a favourable Bournemouth run against Leeds, Ipswich, Forest and Fulham. Van Hecke is a slightly cheaper alternative. Arsenal defenders are better bought from Gameweek 10 rather than before Liverpool away, while Brighton’s attacking defender De Cuyper should be benched at Manchester City and monitored for a possible move to left-back.

Managers should look to move on Nottingham Forest defenders before a difficult run against Brentford, Manchester City, Bournemouth and Chelsea. Tarkowski and Lewis Hall are acceptable short-term holds because of upcoming clean-sheet opportunities, but Tarkowski is poor long-term value. For goalkeepers, Kinsky at £4.4m is the budget buy with strong fixtures, while Raya remains the preferred premium option. Avoid buying players into Gameweek 9 who face Manchester City away, notably De Cuyper, Van Dijk-type defensive punts and Brighton defensive assets; it is a poor entry point even where their longer-term prospects are attractive.
key_points: Buy and captain Erling Haaland in Gameweek 9; he remains the only premium with elite, dependable returns and is viable for the armband through Gameweek 11.
Sell Bukayo Saka after his minimum five-week injury absence, and treat Joao Pedro as a likely sale if his knee issue keeps him out beyond Gameweek 10.
Nicolas Jackson is the leading forward buy, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin a cheaper penalty-taking alternative with secure minutes.
Keep Cole Palmer for Manchester United at home and hold Bryan Mbeumo through Chelsea and Aston Villa rather than reacting to recent blanks.
Prioritise Manzambi in midfield for Aston Villa’s fixture run; Pascal Gross and Tavernier are also strong transfer targets.
Buy Antonio Silva or Van Hecke for Bournemouth’s favourable defensive schedule, with Silva the higher-upside option for contributions and bonus.
Sell or downgrade Nottingham Forest defenders ahead of a difficult Gameweek 9-12 fixture swing, and avoid Manchester United defensive assets.
Bench De Cuyper if owned against Manchester City, monitor his positioning, and avoid buying defenders for a Manchester City away fixture.

items.headline: Haaland is the clear Gameweek 9 captain as Jackson tops a forward-line rebuild
items.summary:
Gameweek 8 leaves the squad carrying three injured bench players — Joao Pedro, Carney Chukwuemeka and Bobby Thomas — after a damaging week compounded by not owning Ezri Konsa. The current XI is set up in a 3-5-2, but the injury situation and an unconvincing Goncalo Guedes make a forward transfer the priority for Gameweek 9.

No move is made early. Midweek cup line-ups, particularly involving Chelsea and Liverpool, and the later Gameweek 9 press conferences are key to assessing both fitness and rotation. Joao Pedro is the main concern, with reports suggesting he could be absent until the international break. If that is confirmed, selling him may justify a -4 hit, but only after the latest news.

Guedes is the likeliest immediate sale despite not being injured. With £1.0m in the bank, any forward is affordable, and Jackson is the preferred replacement ahead of Aston Villa's home fixture against Fulham. If Joao Pedro also needs replacing, Calvert-Lewin or Evanilson are the leading alternatives; buying Jackson for Guedes and Calvert-Lewin for Joao Pedro would also allow Slater to return to the bench rather than start.

Chukwuemeka's trip to Liverpool makes him an easy player to bench while awaiting an update for the following week. Thomas has Sunderland at home and starts over Diaby away at Manchester City if declared fit. Gameweek 9's fixtures are generally uninspiring, but Haaland remains the straightforward captaincy choice, with the plan centred on adding at least one new forward and potentially accepting a hit for a second if Pedro's absence is long-term.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 9 despite an otherwise weak fixture slate.

items.headline: Erling Haaland dominates Gameweek 9 captaincy as João Pedro injury clouds FPL plans
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the standout captain for Gameweek 9 despite Manchester City facing Brighton, largely because the usual alternatives are unconvincing. Haaland has nine goals in eight matches, is delivering almost a goal involvement per game and remains the safest vice-captain whenever managers take a risk elsewhere. Alexander Isak is emerging as the premium alternative, with six goals in seven starts and a favourable Newcastle run beginning in Gameweek 10, although his injury record and Liverpool’s congested schedule remain concerns.

João Pedro’s absence creates the immediate transfer dilemma. Chelsea look markedly less effective without their focal-point forward, but there is no clear timescale on his issue. If he is out for two or more weeks, Nicolas Jackson is the preferred replacement: he costs £6.7m, is in strong form, has improved his all-round play and begins an exceptional Aston Villa fixture run from Gameweek 9, including Fulham, Manchester United, Sunderland, Ipswich, Everton and Crystal Palace. Managers are advised to wait for injury updates where possible, but Pedro-to-Jackson is the straightforward move for those forced to act.

The midfield premium structure is under review. Cole Palmer’s red card and long spell of underwhelming returns make him expendable, particularly with cheaper Chelsea routes such as Morgan Rogers and João Pedro available when fit. Selling Palmer or Bukayo Saka, who is sidelined for several weeks, can fund Haaland, Isak and Arsenal defender Gabriel. Gabriel is increasingly viewed as a premium defensive option because of his secure starts, clean-sheet potential, DefCon points and set-piece threat, even if his price remains high.

Defensive injuries leave several managers short-handed, with Riccardo Calafiori, Nico Williams and Bobby Thomas all flagged. Nico Williams posts a positive update after his knock and remains worth holding if fit, while Joško Gvardiol continues to offer major attacking upside despite rotation risk. For dependable budget options, Antonín Silva, Joe Rodon, Jaka Bijol, Bobby Thomas and Vuskovic offer strong DefCon routes, while Leeds’ Mormović is highlighted as a likely season-long hold due to his defensive points, assists and occasional attacking threat.

Fixture planning points strongly towards Aston Villa, Bournemouth and Leeds. Villa’s six-match run from Gameweek 9 is among the best available, driving interest in Jackson and Manzambi, while Bournemouth assets such as Evanilson, Tavernier, Ryan and Silva benefit from matches against Leeds, Ipswich, Nottingham Forest, Fulham, Brighton and Hull. Isak becomes especially attractive from Gameweek 10, while Gameweek 12 is a potential Free Hit week for managers with chips because Arsenal play Manchester City and Haaland has a less obvious captaincy case.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 9 against Brighton, with Jackson the preferred vice-captain if João Pedro is sold for him.
Sell João Pedro for Nicolas Jackson if injury news suggests an absence of at least two weeks; Jackson’s Gameweek 9-14 fixtures are outstanding.
Alexander Isak is the leading premium target from Gameweek 10, but managers should account for his fitness history and Liverpool’s tight schedule.
Cole Palmer is increasingly a sell candidate, as moving to a cheaper midfielder can fund Haaland, Isak and Gabriel.
Gabriel is a viable premium defender due to secure minutes, DefCon reliability, clean-sheet potential and set-piece threat.
Hold Nico Williams if declared fit, while monitoring Calafiori and Bobby Thomas closely before making defensive transfers.
Bournemouth attackers and defenders gain appeal through a strong six-game run, with Evanilson, Tavernier, Ryan and Antonín Silva all under consideration.

items.headline: João Pedro owners urged to wait as Jackson tops Gameweek 9 replacement list
items.summary:
João Pedro is the second-most-owned player in FPL and a major doubt ahead of Gameweek 9, but an immediate sale is not automatic. Gameweek 11 is still around a month away, so even a several-week absence may be manageable if managers have a playable bench and expect him back in November. The key advice is to wait for further fitness information before committing to a transfer.

For managers who do need to sell, Jackson is the leading replacement. Priced at around £6.7m, he has an attractive longer-term fixture run and is impressing through his link-up play with Manzambi. Aston Villa’s European schedule adds some rotation and fatigue risk, but Gameweek 9 is viewed as a strong entry point for a forward with favourable fixtures ahead.

Evanilson ranks next because Bournemouth’s long-term schedule is excellent. The Brazilian is producing returns, playing well in tandem with Tavernier and offers a relatively affordable route into Bournemouth’s attack at a little over £6m. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is also a viable option: Leeds have no European commitments, he remains their central goal threat and the fixture list is broadly favourable, although difficult away matches temper the appeal.

Alexander Isak is a higher-priced alternative for managers freed from underperforming premium midfielders such as Morgan Gibbs-White, Bryan Mbeumo and Cole Palmer. Arsenal in Gameweek 9 is an awkward immediate fixture, but Liverpool’s run from Gameweek 10 becomes far more attractive. Thierno Barry is the fifth option; recent team scoring has been modest, yet he ranks second in the Premier League for big chances behind only Erling Haaland and has a promising set of fixtures coming up.
key_points: Do not automatically sell João Pedro before receiving clearer injury news; a playable bench can make a short-term hold worthwhile.
Jackson is the preferred João Pedro replacement at roughly £6.7m, with favourable long-term fixtures outweighing Aston Villa’s European commitments.
Evanilson offers strong value at just over £6m as Bournemouth enter an excellent extended fixture run.
Dominic Calvert-Lewin is Leeds’ main attacking threat and benefits from having no European rotation risk.
Alexander Isak is best considered for Gameweek 10 onwards, as Arsenal in Gameweek 9 is a difficult short-term fixture but Liverpool’s subsequent schedule improves.
Thierno Barry is a differential option with elite big-chance volume, ranking behind only Erling Haaland despite his side’s recent lack of goals.

items.title: FPL PLAYERS TO BUY | GW9 ✅ JOAO PEDRO INJURED ⚠️
items.headline: Erling Haaland leads Gameweek 9 captaincy as Aston Villa and Bournemouth assets rise
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the standout captain for Gameweek 9 at home to Brighton, topping the projected points among all players. Manchester City’s forward is joined by Thiago, Nicolas Jackson and Dominic Solanke near the top of the forward projections, but Jackson is the preferred replacement if João Pedro’s injury proves serious. Chelsea’s update suggests Pedro has a fluid issue and could be absent for up to two gameweeks; because an international break follows, holding him is viable if he misses only those two rounds and a squad has cover. On a Wildcard, the preferred front three is Haaland, Jackson and Barry, whose 5.6m price, home fixture against Coventry and strong underlying xG make him a high-upside budget gamble despite concerns over finishing.

Aston Villa’s turnaround and fixture run make their assets increasingly attractive. After taking one point from their opening four matches, Villa have returned three wins and a draw from the next four, and now face Fulham, Manchester United, Sunderland, Ipswich, Everton and Crystal Palace before tougher meetings with Chelsea, Leeds and Liverpool. Suzuki is a notable goalkeeper option for Villa’s home match with Fulham, while Villa defenders merit longer-term consideration. However, Kinsky at 4.4m is the leading budget goalkeeper: Tottenham’s defence has been more reliable than results and criticism suggest, with Pedro Porro’s return strengthening a back line that faces Palace, Leeds, Ipswich, Sunderland and Fulham. Avoid spending transfers on minor goalkeeper swaps unless upgrading to Arsenal’s David Raya or reacting to a clear defensive collapse.

Bournemouth defenders are also priority buys, particularly ahead of Leeds at home. Silva is favoured at 5.0m over the more expensive alternatives because Bournemouth rank well defensively and the small projected difference between their centre-backs does not justify an extra 0.5m. Pedro Porro and Van Hecke rate highly for the coming weeks, while Gabriel remains the premium defensive safety pick after his 17-point haul against Everton, albeit at 7.9m. Arsenal have the league’s best xG-conceded record, but buying their defenders immediately before Liverpool away is less appealing unless on a Wildcard. Longer term, Vaskovic and Mohammadovic are also identified as strong defensive options once their difficult immediate fixtures pass.

Midfield offers limited excitement, and Gameweek 9 is not considered a strong Free Hit opportunity unless a team has five or six unavailable players. A more promising early Free Hit target is Gameweek 14, when Bournemouth play Hull, Leeds host Ipswich, Manchester United host Coventry and Villa host Palace; it could also allow managers to move temporarily away from Arsenal assets against Tottenham and even Haaland against Brentford. Gibbs-White remains a hold despite poor recent returns because his underlying involvement is strong and Forest have badly underperformed at both ends. Gross and D-Kyper are bench candidates against Manchester City if squad depth permits, while Sunderland picks are avoided as European, League Cup and Premier League commitments raise rotation and fatigue concerns.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 9 for Brighton at home, where he leads all projected scorers.
Wait for the midweek League Cup matches before confirming transfers, with Arsenal, Manchester City, Liverpool, Chelsea, Newcastle, Villa, Tottenham and several other clubs in action.
Sell João Pedro for Nicolas Jackson if the Chelsea forward is ruled out for more than two Gameweeks; otherwise, benching Pedro through the short absence is a viable plan.
Target Aston Villa’s run from Gameweek 9 through mid-December, beginning with Fulham, but plan to move their assets on before Chelsea, Leeds and Liverpool.
Buy Bournemouth defender Silva for Leeds at home rather than paying extra for a marginally higher-priced team-mate.
Kinsky is the preferred 4.4m budget goalkeeper, while Suzuki is an alternative for Villa’s favourable run; avoid routine goalkeeper transfers unless upgrading to Raya.
Do not Free Hit in Gameweek 9 in most cases; Gameweek 14 has greater fixture-based upside.
Bench Gross and D-Kyper against Manchester City if possible, and retain Gibbs-White despite his recent points drought because his underlying numbers remain encouraging.

items.headline: Palmer holds for now, but Gabriel and Tavernier shape Gameweek 9 plans
items.summary:
Cole Palmer is available to face Manchester United at home in Gameweek 9 despite his red card against Spurs, because he serves his one-match ban in the Carabao Cup. He is expected to start if fit after a useful rest, and Chelsea's run through Gameweek 13 remains acceptable: Manchester United, Sunderland, Leeds, Forest and Palace. However, Palmer's underlying numbers are poor for a £9.8m midfielder and he is not currently justifying the price. Holding is preferred for managers with only one or two free transfers, but selling becomes reasonable for those with spare moves and a clear use for the funds, particularly to reach Gabriel or Isak.

João Pedro's fitness is the immediate transfer issue. The injury appears to be related to his previous knee problem, although the length of absence is not yet confirmed. A one-week absence is an easy bench, while two weeks can still be manageable given the international break and Chelsea's long-term fixture appeal; a longer lay-off makes a sale more compelling, especially with Liverpool and Manchester City in Gameweeks 14 and 15. Nicolas Jackson is the leading replacement thanks to Aston Villa's strong run through Gameweek 15 and his secure role, while Isak offers Liverpool attack upside from Gameweek 10 but is expensive for a forward without penalties. Evanilson, Barry and other cheaper forwards can free funds for defensive upgrades, though Evanilson faces some possible minutes risk with Kroupi returning.

Arsenal's defence remains central to planning. Gabriel is the premium target at £7.9m: he is nailed for league minutes, carries major set-piece threat and offers the security missing from Riccardo Calafiori and Cristhian Kzer. Calafiori's minor issue requires monitoring, and he is worth holding through Liverpool away in Gameweek 9 if fit, with Hull at home in Gameweek 10 an attractive fixture. But his recurring rotation risk around European and midweek league matches means a future switch to Gabriel is sensible. Kzer is exceptional value at £4.7m for existing owners while Saliba is absent, but non-owners should not buy before Liverpool away given the uncertainty over Saliba's return and Kzer's longer-term place.

Bruno Fernandes is the priority sale for most owners after being benched for the full Gameweek 8 match and returning only once all season at £11.7m. His funds can improve multiple positions or help finance Haaland, Gabriel or Isak. The narrow exception is a Haaland-owning squad with no other problems: a managerial change at Manchester United could restore Bruno immediately, though he is not a player to buy. Ryan Cherki is also a sell when a spare transfer is available because Manchester City minutes are too unpredictable. In contrast, Marcus Tavernier is the preferred affordable midfield buy at £6.3m, with five goals, strong underlying numbers, 83 average minutes per start and a favourable Bournemouth run from Leeds at home to Hull at home across the next six. Manzambi is a viable alternative with even better Aston Villa fixtures but less reliable minutes.

For Gameweek 9, Haaland is the captain against Brighton at home. A sample squad carries three free transfers but likely needs only one, with João Pedro and Calafiori flagged and Sangari uncertain to start. If the Chelsea and Arsenal flags prove short term, Sangari to Tavernier or Manzambi is the likely move to provide cover while preserving transfers. If João Pedro or Calafiori is ruled out for longer, the plan shifts toward a cheaper forward, Jackson, or using released money to upgrade Calafiori to Gabriel.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Brighton at home in Gameweek 9.
Hold Palmer for Manchester United at home unless spare transfers are needed to redirect his £9.8m price elsewhere; his cup suspension does not rule him out of the league match.
Bench João Pedro for one week if possible, consider covering him for two, but sell if the knee issue becomes a longer absence.
Nicolas Jackson is the leading João Pedro replacement due to Aston Villa's excellent Gameweeks 9-15 schedule, while cheaper forwards can create funds for Gabriel.
Gabriel is the preferred long-term Arsenal defender because he is nailed and dangerous from set pieces; Calafiori is a hold for now but a likely future sell due to rotation.
Do not buy Kzer before Liverpool away in Gameweek 9, despite his £4.7m value, unless Saliba's absence becomes clearer and longer term.
Sell Bruno Fernandes in most squads after his Gameweek 8 benching; only strong Haaland-owning teams with no urgent issues can justify waiting for a Manchester United managerial bounce.
Tavernier is the standout cheap midfield transfer at £6.3m, while Manzambi is a close alternative with stronger fixtures but less secure minutes.

items.title: GW8 Is Over... Here's What I'm Doing in GW9!
items.headline: Marcos Silva becomes the standout Gameweek 9 defensive buy as Bournemouth’s clean-sheet run gathers pace
items.summary:
Gameweek 8 is unusually volatile, with many popular assets blanking or missing out: João Pedro and Riccardo Calafiori do not feature, Cole Palmer is sent off, and major sides including Manchester United, Chelsea, Brighton and Manchester City disappoint. A 52-point score is therefore a respectable green-arrow return in a week where Arsenal defenders, especially Gabriel and Konsa, provide most of the accessible points. Managers should avoid overreacting to low-owned one-week hauls and instead focus on fixture runs and injury news before Gameweek 9.

The key squad decisions depend on João Pedro, Calafiori and Bobby Thomas. João Pedro has a recurrence of fluid around his knee and is a sell if the absence extends beyond one match, particularly with stronger forward options emerging. Calafiori reportedly has only a minor issue, and his Liverpool away fixture in Gameweek 9 makes him an easy bench candidate if necessary; he is worth retaining if fit again for Arsenal’s Gameweek 10 meeting with Hull. Thomas also needs assessment after going off before 60 minutes, but his later fixtures, including Crystal Palace and Ipswich at home, make a short-term hold reasonable.

Aston Villa and Bournemouth are the principal teams to target through Gameweek 16. Villa begin with Fulham, Manchester United, Sunderland and Ipswich, making Nicolas Jackson the leading João Pedro replacement after his strong recent form and improved confidence. Alexander Isak is another high-upside option despite Arsenal in Gameweek 9: Liverpool’s attack is improving, Bradley Barker adds creativity, and Isak may retain penalties while Salah is absent. Barry is worth keeping for Newcastle and Coventry, while Calvert-Lewin has less appealing immediate fixtures. Evanilson is avoided because Kroupi Jr.’s return creates serious uncertainty over Bournemouth’s striker and attacking-midfield minutes.

At the back, Bournemouth’s Marcos Silva is the preferred target. He combines frequent defensive-contribution points, some set-piece and aerial threat, and a favourable run against Leeds, Nottingham Forest, Fulham, Ipswich, Coventry and Hull. Bournemouth rank second only to Arsenal for projected clean sheets over the next six gameweeks, so Silva offers a reliable points floor alongside upside. Van Hecke is also viable on fixtures, while Gabriel remains attractive for managers with spare funds. A possible two-transfer move is João Pedro to Isak and an injured defender to Silva, but if Pedro or Calafiori is only absent briefly, selling De Cuyper for Silva is an alternative. De Cuyper’s second-half deployment at left-back, even before Brighton’s returning wingers are available, raises a minutes and attacking-output warning.
key_points: Cole Palmer’s red-card ban is served in the League Cup against Liverpool, so he remains available for Chelsea’s Gameweek 9 trip to Manchester United.
Sell João Pedro if his knee issue rules him out for multiple weeks; Nicolas Jackson is the standout replacement, with Alexander Isak the premium alternative.
Hold Calafiori if the injury is short-term, as Arsenal face Hull in Gameweek 10 after Liverpool away and remain the league’s strongest defensive unit.
Marcos Silva is the leading defender target because Bournemouth pair excellent fixtures with high projected clean-sheet odds and his dependable defensive-contribution floor.
Avoid rushing into Evanilson: Kroupi Jr.’s return threatens his Premier League role, while Leeds away is not an ideal immediate fixture.
De Cuyper to Silva is under consideration because De Cuyper plays at left-back after Brighton’s substitution and faces future competition from returning wide players.
Barry is retained for Gameweeks 9-10 against Newcastle and Coventry, with Newcastle still conceding significant chances despite their clean sheet.
Wait for press-conference news on João Pedro, Calafiori and Bobby Thomas before committing transfers in a difficult Gameweek 9 fixture slate.

items.title: I captained Palmer for a red card 😭 FPL Kneejerk Gameweek 9 🔥
items.headline: Haaland is the clear Gameweek 9 captain as João Pedro and Calafiori dominate transfer plans
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the standout captain for Gameweek 9 despite Manchester City facing Brighton. The alternative captaincy options lack the same combination of security and upside: Nicolas Jackson has Fulham at home after scoring twice, while Cole Palmer has Manchester United at home, but Haaland remains on penalties and is the safest premium pick. Palmer’s red card does not rule him out of the league match because he serves his one-game suspension in the Carabao Cup; he is a hold rather than an urgent sale, even if his recent output has not justified his price.

The most pressing squad issue is João Pedro, whose recurring knee problem may keep him out against Manchester United. If he misses only one Gameweek, the preferred approach is to bench him and use a playable substitute rather than force a transfer. If the absence looks likely to extend to two matches or beyond the international break, selling becomes more appealing, particularly given the risk of repeated fitness issues. Nicolas Jackson and Evanilson are the leading direct replacements, with Jackson offering an excellent Aston Villa fixture run but some substitution risk and no penalties; Dominic Calvert-Lewin remains a viable hold because he is nailed and on penalties.

Riccardo Calafiori is another player to monitor rather than immediately sell. Arsenal’s Liverpool trip in Gameweek 9 makes him easy to bench if necessary, and a midweek appearance could clarify whether he is fit for Gameweek 10. However, rotation is now a genuine concern, making Gabriel the safer long-term Arsenal defender if funds allow. A move to a Tottenham defender, particularly Pedro Porro or a cheaper defensive-contribution option, is also under consideration, but there is little reason to rush before more team news arrives.

In midfield, Sander Berge/Sangaré-type budget enablers are the likeliest upgrades for managers with spare transfers. Marcus Tavernier is the preferred low-cost target because Bournemouth’s fixtures and his role are reliable, although he is not first-choice on penalties when other takers are on the pitch. Aston Villa’s Manzambi is a cheaper, more speculative alternative with strong fixtures but greater uncertainty over minutes, while Mohammed Kudus is an interesting differential as Tottenham enter a favourable run beginning with Crystal Palace at home. The wider advice is to avoid panic after a low-scoring Gameweek 8: many popular players disappoint, Gameweek 10 squads look stronger on paper, and waiting through midweek cup matches and Friday updates is prudent.

A Gameweek 9 Free Hit is possible for teams overloaded with poor fixtures, flags and non-starters, but it is not a priority. The best teams still rely heavily on Haaland and Tottenham players, while many attractive sides play each other and the pool of explosive one-week picks is limited. Managers should use the chip only if it materially fixes multiple immediate issues, not simply in reaction to a bad Gameweek.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Brighton in Gameweek 9; Jackson and Palmer are acceptable alternatives but do not match Haaland’s security or penalty upside.
Palmer serves his red-card ban in the Carabao Cup and is available against Manchester United in Gameweek 9, so he is not an urgent transfer out.
Wait for João Pedro injury news: hold if he misses one match, but consider selling if his knee issue is likely to rule him out for two or more Gameweeks.
Jackson and Evanilson are the main João Pedro replacements, while Calvert-Lewin remains a reasonable hold due to secure minutes and penalties.
Do not rush to sell Calafiori before Liverpool; assess his midweek involvement, with Gabriel the safer long-term Arsenal defensive option if rotation persists.
Tavernier is the preferred budget-midfield move, with Manzambi offering a cheaper but less proven alternative and Kudus a Tottenham differential.
Avoid early transfers where possible because Carabao Cup matches and pending injury updates could create further problems before the deadline.
A Gameweek 9 Free Hit is viable only for heavily damaged squads; it is not compelling enough to use merely because of Gameweek 8 frustration.

items.title: FPL GW9 TRANSFER PLANS ✅ MY GAMEWEEK 9 TEAM 🎯
items.headline: Hold João Pedro through the break as Silva becomes the Gameweek 9 defensive transfer
items.summary:
A 45-point Gameweek 8 is salvaged by Erling Haaland captaincy and Ezri Konsa’s 14-point haul, but João Pedro’s injury, Cole Palmer’s red card and Riccardo Calafiori’s benching create fresh selection issues. Palmer, Morgan Rogers and João Pedro combine for no points, although Palmer is available for Chelsea’s Gameweek 9 home match against Manchester United because he serves his suspension in the midweek cup tie. Chelsea’s strong attacking projection and that home fixture make Palmer and Rogers holds rather than immediate sales.

João Pedro is the key decision. Aston Villa’s Ollie Watkins alternative, Jackson, costs only £6.7m and has an appealing run of Fulham, Manchester United, Sunderland, Ipswich, Everton and Crystal Palace, while Alexander Isak is also in form with six goals in seven starts. However, if João Pedro’s apparent recurrence of a three-week injury only rules him out for Gameweeks 9 and 10 before the international break, selling him creates an awkward need to buy him back soon afterwards. With only one free transfer, the preference is to hold João Pedro unless the absence proves longer or there are multiple free transfers available.

The planned move is therefore to sell Chiao for Bournemouth’s Silva. Silva, priced at £5.0m, is viewed as a potentially long-term defender because Bournemouth remain strong defensively despite European commitments, while his defensive-contribution potential adds another route to points. The transfer also preserves flexibility for future issues, including possible changes to Konsa or Bart Verbruggen when other defenders return, and a possible move for Vuskovic after the international break.

Arsenal defenders remain worth holding despite a difficult Liverpool trip. Gabriel’s 17-point haul takes him to 52 points, behind only Haaland among forwards and only Gross among midfielders, reinforcing his set-and-forget appeal. Calafiori should be kept for now despite a minor hip or rib concern and rotation risk from Myles Lewis-Skelly; reassess after Arsenal’s midweek Champions League match. Spurs also become attractive defensive assets: they rank second for projected clean sheets and face Crystal Palace, Leeds, Ipswich, Sunderland and Fulham, making Guglielmo Vicario/Kinsky and Van Hecke viable holds or buys.

For the Gameweek 9 XI, Raya starts behind Mendy, Chiao and Van Hecke, with Gross, Bryan Mbeumo, Palmer, Rogers and Sharda in midfield and Haaland up front. João Pedro is provisionally benched due to injury. The closest call is Gross away to Manchester City versus Konsa away to Liverpool: Gross offers attacking-return upside against a City defence that still concedes chances, while Konsa’s route is primarily defensive contributions or an unlikely Arsenal clean sheet at Anfield.
key_points: Captain Haaland over Palmer is rewarded in Gameweek 8, while Palmer is available to face Manchester United in Gameweek 9 after serving his ban in the cup.
Hold João Pedro if his injury absence is limited to Gameweeks 9 and 10; the international break reduces the value of selling and rebuying him.
Jackson is the leading João Pedro replacement for managers with spare transfers, with Aston Villa entering an excellent fixture run and the forward priced at £6.7m.
Sell Chiao for Bournemouth’s £5.0m Silva with the available free transfer, prioritising a durable defensive hold and preserving future flexibility.
Keep Palmer and Rogers despite their blanks, as Chelsea rank highly for projected goals and host Manchester United next.
Hold Calafiori for now and reassess after Arsenal’s midweek European match; Gabriel remains the standout Arsenal defensive asset despite the Liverpool fixture.
Spurs defenders and goalkeeper options improve sharply, with Palace, Leeds, Ipswich, Sunderland and Fulham in their next five fixtures.
Van Hecke is a viable defensive buy, while Gross versus Konsa is the main Gameweek 9 benching dilemma.

items.title: HORROR GAMEWEEK 😭 3 INJURIES! ⚠️ MY FPL GW9 TRANSFER PLANS 📝 Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Gonzalo Garcia exit tops Gameweek 9 plans as João Pedro injury leaves squad stretched
items.summary:
A disastrous Gameweek 8 sends the squad outside the top one million after Cole Palmer's red card, Pascal Groß's own goal, a Diaper one-pointer and blanks from Morgan Gibbs-White. The biggest rank damage comes from not owning Ezri Konsa, whose 14-point haul punishes a defensive setup built around David Raya and Riccardo Calafiori instead. Van Hecke's bench points compound the frustration, while Bobby Thomas, Calafiori and João Pedro are all flagged ahead of Gameweek 9.

The immediate priority is to wait for injury news rather than chase early price changes. Calafiori may return soon and is not essential away to Liverpool, though he is wanted for Hull at home in Gameweek 10. Bobby Thomas is a hold unless reports confirm a long-term absence, while João Pedro is the key decision: if he is back after the international break he can be retained, but a recurrence or extended lay-off makes him a sell. His absence also weakens the appeal of Palmer and Morgan Rogers, although Palmer serves his suspension in the cup and remains available against Manchester United.

Provided at least one of the flagged players is available, Gonzalo Garcia is the preferred sale. He is not secure for minutes, has not delivered goals and should not be needed in the starting XI again. Jackson is the leading replacement because of an excellent run against Fulham, Manchester United, Sunderland, Ipswich, Everton, Crystal Palace and Coventry, although his minutes and lack of penalties temper the enthusiasm. Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Evanilson are the next options, with Calvert-Lewin narrowly preferred; Alexander Isak is attractive from Gameweek 10 but is difficult to fund without selling Palmer.

A hit becomes viable only if João Pedro is confirmed out for several weeks, allowing two forward moves or a Pedro downgrade to fund a Slater upgrade to Tavernier or Manzambi. Palmer, Gibbs-White, Groß and the defensive rotation are not urgent fixes despite their flaws. A Gameweek 9 Free Hit is also rejected: the fixture list lacks standout targets, clean-sheet odds are modest, and the players worth targeting from Aston Villa, Brentford and Spurs are largely useful long-term anyway. Haaland remains captain, with the plan to preserve flexibility until late press conferences and midweek cup matches clarify the injury picture.
key_points: Erling Haaland is the Gameweek 9 captain despite Manchester City's home match against Brighton offering few obvious attacking alternatives beyond him.
Wait until late in the week for updates on João Pedro, Riccardo Calafiori and Bobby Thomas; early transfers are too risky with only one free move.
Gonzalo Garcia is the leading transfer out if any of the flagged players can return, with Jackson the most likely replacement.
Jackson has the strongest fixture run but carries minutes and penalty concerns; Dominic Calvert-Lewin ranks ahead of Evanilson as the alternative.
Sell João Pedro only if his injury is long-term or recurrent; if he returns after the international break, holding is preferred.
Cole Palmer is available against Manchester United because his one-match ban is served in the cup, but João Pedro's absence reduces Palmer's value.
A minus four is only under consideration if João Pedro is ruled out for weeks and a second forward transfer is needed.
Do not Free Hit in Gameweek 9: fixture projections are weak and Villa, Brentford and Spurs assets are better acquired as longer-term picks.

items.title: GABRIEL HAUL 🔥 | FPL CHAI'S GW9 TEAM SELECTION | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Nicolas Jackson emerges as the premium forward target as João Pedro injury reshapes Gameweek 9 plans
items.summary:
Nicolas Jackson is the leading transfer target after a strong two-goal display for Aston Villa against Manchester City, particularly with João Pedro absent and Calvert-Lewin carrying an injury concern. Jackson’s appeal lies in his secure role, frequent involvement in chances and Villa’s improving attack under Unai Emery, with Manzambi, Buendia and McGinn supplying him. His £6.6m-plus price makes a direct switch difficult from cheaper forwards such as Gonzalo García or Thierno Barry, but managers who can find the funds are encouraged to consider him over cheaper midfield alternatives.

Arsenal’s defensive assets remain central to the strategy after Gabriel combines a clean sheet, goal, defensive-contribution points and bonus against Aston Villa. Gabriel’s set-piece threat is the decisive factor: Arsenal create plenty of corners and he remains one of the most reliable starters in the side. Calafiori’s fitness is a concern, but Gabriel is viewed as a priority long-term purchase, potentially funded by downgrading Cole Palmer to a cheaper midfielder such as Amadou Onana or Tavernier. Arsenal face Liverpool in Gameweek 9, however, so managers do not need to force the move immediately if it requires a hit.

João Pedro’s injury puts Chelsea’s attacking assets under scrutiny. Palmer and Rogers are considered strong picks only when João Pedro is available, as Chelsea look far less coherent without their usual front three. Palmer has unconvincing recent underlying numbers and fails the eye test, despite a reasonable fixture run that includes Manchester United, Sunderland, Leeds and Crystal Palace. Selling Palmer for a Villa midfielder or using him to fund Gabriel is viable if João Pedro’s absence is confirmed as more than short term; Bryan Mbeumo is also preferred by some as Manchester United may improve under a new manager.

Gameweek 9 is expected to be low scoring, with Arsenal playing Liverpool and Brighton facing Manchester City, so a Free Hit is not strongly recommended. There are limited standout targets beyond Spurs, Villa and Bournemouth, and the likely gain over a normal team may only be 5-10 points. Holding the chip for injury disruption, festive rotation, or fixture clusters around Gameweeks 12 and 14 offers greater upside. Bench Boost planning points towards Gameweek 11, but only if injuries to João Pedro, Calafiori and others clear up.

Fulham’s back-to-back clean sheets make Bernd Leno and budget defender Joachim Andersen-style options acceptable bench holds, while Aleksandar Mitrović offers a decent defensive-contribution floor at £4.5m. Gonzalo García is more worrying because of his early substitutions and uncertain starting security, despite Fulham’s improved performances. Barry remains a hold for his minutes, penalties and upcoming fixtures, while Pascal Groß and De Cuyper are legitimate starters rather than automatic bench players against a vulnerable Manchester City defence.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland remains the safe Gameweek 9 choice, while Cole Palmer is a high-risk differential captain against Manchester United.
Nicolas Jackson is the preferred replacement for João Pedro or Calvert-Lewin if managers can afford his price point.
Gabriel is a priority Arsenal defender because of clean-sheet potential, defensive-contribution points and sustained set-piece threat.
Monitor João Pedro closely: if he is out for an extended spell, Chelsea midfielders Palmer and Rogers become much less attractive.
Do not rush to Free Hit in Gameweek 9; difficult fixtures across the template make a low-scoring week likely for most managers.
A Gameweek 11 Bench Boost is a viable plan, but only with confirmed fitness for João Pedro, Calafiori and the rest of the bench.
Gonzalo García is a transfer-out candidate due to repeated early substitutions, whereas Thierno Barry is worth holding for minutes, penalties and fixtures.
Fulham defenders and Leno are reasonable budget bench options after consecutive clean sheets, but Villa are still expected to score in Gameweek 9.

items.title: Calvert-Lewin is a DOUBT 😱 FPL Gameweek 8 Deadline Stream 🚀 Transfer made 🔒
items.headline: Palmer gets the armband over Haaland as Calvert-Lewin fitness clouds Gameweek 8
items.summary:
Cole Palmer is the final captaincy call for Gameweek 8, despite Erling Haaland being the safer, more popular option away at Aston Villa. Haaland has blanked only once this season and remains the default captain for managers who want to minimise risk, but Palmer at home to Tottenham offers a high-upside differential. The concern is that Palmer's recent underlying numbers and consistency have been underwhelming, while Spurs have looked more defensively solid than their reputation suggests. Even so, the combination of home advantage, penalties and low captaincy ownership makes Palmer worth the calculated risk.

The only transfer is Dominik Szoboszlai to Bryan Mbeumo, made early to remove an injured midfield issue and secure a reliable longer-term attacking option. Mbeumo is preferred over alternatives such as Morgan Gibbs-White, Antoine Semenyo, Marcus Tavernier and Dango Ouattara/Sharda-type budget picks because there is no immediate need for the extra cash. Gibbs-White, Tavernier, Rogers and Sharda remain viable Saka replacements depending on budget and squad structure, but there is no need to force additional moves simply because funds are available.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is orange-flagged with a bruised foot and is a serious doubt, although he is not ruled out. The approach is to start him rather than spend a transfer on a one-week replacement, accepting the risk that he could make a short substitute appearance. If he misses out, Sangare is first in line from the bench, with Van Hecke also available. Gross starts despite Liverpool away, largely because he is a nailed penalty taker and remains a strong long-term asset from Gameweek 10; Sangare is benched after uncertainty around his minutes. Lewis Hall starts ahead of Brighton's de Cuyper, although de Cuyper's left-wing role makes him a credible alternative rather than a straightforward defensive bench option.

Potential storm disruption does not justify transfers, hits or a Free Hit. Liverpool v Brighton is the main fixture being discussed as a possible weather risk, but there is no firm indication of a postponement. Managers with Brighton or Liverpool players should monitor late news, but rolling transfers is preferable to reshaping a squad around an unconfirmed cancellation. The wider strategy is to preserve flexibility, carry free transfers where possible and target the stronger fixture run beginning around Gameweek 10 rather than chase short-term punts.
key_points: Cole Palmer is captained at home to Tottenham, with Haaland the safer but less differential alternative away at Aston Villa.
Szoboszlai is sold for Bryan Mbeumo; no further transfer is made before the deadline.
Calvert-Lewin starts despite a bruised-foot doubt, with Sangare first substitute if he is absent.
Gross starts at Liverpool because of his security and penalty role, while Sangare is benched amid residual minutes concerns.
Lewis Hall starts ahead of de Cuyper, although de Cuyper's advanced left-wing role means benching him is a close call.
Do not use transfers, hits or a Free Hit purely to cover the unconfirmed weather threat to Liverpool v Brighton.
Raya is viewed as an excellent long-term goalkeeper, but upgrading Kinsky/Verbruggen is optional rather than urgent given improving fixtures ahead.

items.title: FPL GW8 DEADLINE LIVE! ⏰ Transfers, Team News & Wildcard 🚨 | Get Your Last Minute FPL Questions In!
items.headline: Haaland stays captain as Saka injury and storm risk push FPL managers towards Brentford depth
items.summary:
Erling Haaland remains the straightforward captaincy pick for Gameweek 8 after another strong run of form, despite viable Chelsea alternatives. Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro are the main alternatives, with Joao Pedro preferred for a safer non-Haaland route because of his open-play involvement, while Palmer offers greater haul potential through penalties and set pieces. Haaland’s vice-captain should ideally come from a southern-based side, most likely Chelsea, given weather concerns around several northern fixtures.

Bukayo Saka is an immediate sell after suffering a quadriceps problem. He misses Gameweek 8 and could be absent for around six weeks, although the precise prognosis depends on further scans. Palmer or Morgan Rogers are the preferred direct replacements for managers who do not own them, followed by Bryan Mbeumo; Morgan Gibbs-White, Kevin Schade and Antoine Semenyo-priced alternatives such as Tavernier are cheaper routes. Martin Odegaard, however, is a hold rather than a Saka replacement target: Saka’s absence increases Odegaard’s set-piece and penalty responsibility, making him a better asset rather than a player to sell.

The key late concern is severe UK weather. Coventry v Fulham and Sunderland v Leeds appear the most exposed fixtures, while Hull v Brentford, Liverpool v Brighton and Manchester United v Bournemouth are also under weather warnings. Postponements remain unlikely, but managers with shallow benches are advised to use available free transfers if they can improve cover rather than carrying injured or non-playing assets. Bench Boost is best avoided because even a small postponement risk undermines the chip’s value.

The final squad moves are Kinsky and Saka to David Raya and Mbeumo, followed by Soule to Schade. Schade starts ahead of Thomas Asante, with Thomas first substitute, then Diego Coppola and Barry. Raya, Calafiori and Arsenal defensive coverage remain attractive over a longer run despite the risk that a single lost clean sheet hurts a triple-up in one gameweek. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is doubtful and may not start, but is generally worth holding rather than selling; managers can start him if their bench is adequate or play a safer alternative such as Pascal Gross. Phil Foden is available but looks too risky to buy amid uncertain Manchester City minutes, while Matheus Nunes and Cherki are similarly less secure than established options.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 8, with Joao Pedro or Cole Palmer the leading alternatives and a Chelsea-based vice-captain sensible amid weather concerns.
Sell Bukayo Saka after his quad injury; a potential six-week absence makes Palmer, Rogers or Mbeumo the leading replacements.
Keep Martin Odegaard if owned, as Saka’s absence likely improves his penalty and set-piece share.
Avoid Bench Boost because Coventry v Fulham and Sunderland v Leeds face the greatest postponement risk, with other northern fixtures also affected by storm warnings.
Use spare free transfers to add bench depth rather than carrying unavailable players, especially if your squad contains multiple Fulham, Coventry, Sunderland or Leeds assets.
Hold Dominic Calvert-Lewin if possible despite his doubtful status; his replacement options are not compelling and his availability may be clearer closer to Sunday.
Schade is the preferred short-term midfield addition over Tavernier, while Mbeumo is the stronger option if budget allows.
Avoid buying Foden for Gameweek 8 because his starting prospects are uncertain despite being fit.
